best_idea: Give each fight one bounded input queue that the tick drains whole once per fixed step, drop and count overflow instead of blocking or stopping the fight, and treat a join or engage as reserved until the server confirms it, expiring it on a deadline.
decision_why: The one-writer tick with a bounded, drained-per-tick input queue is what a server-tick row needs, and the join reservation fits the rule that a join counts only once confirmed; adapt because the donor drops the NEWEST input and disconnects every player when the call queue fills, and it truncates its deadline to whole seconds, so we keep the shape and change those three rules.
acceptance: A server test sends 200 input messages in one tick interval into a 128-slot fight queue and asserts the tick processes exactly the queued batch once, the overflow is counted per session, and the fight keeps running; a join that is not confirmed within a 1.5 s deadline (at 60 Hz) is removed at its deadline tick, not 15-30 s later.
